$comment: The one record of what makes CI run its thorough and live lanes, and which jobs those are.
Read by scripts/thorough-inputs.mjs (the `gate` job), scripts/ci-gate.mjs (the `ci-gate` job) and
tests/Infrastructure/CiWorkflowDriftTests.cs. thoroughInputs: an entry ending in `/` is a prefix,
one containing `*` is a glob (`**` spans directories), anything else is an exact path; every entry
must match a tracked file, which scripts/thorough-inputs.test.mjs asserts, so a renamed input cannot
leave a dead entry behind. A layer that creates a new input adds it here in the same change.

thoroughInputs.why: pins what the frozen suites replay: the NR client HAR, the NR Editor snapshot and the BattleScribe app build (#301 merged green on kitchen-sink and broke two of them)
IKVM recompiles the BattleScribe engine and Playwright ships the browser every NR UI driver drives (#503)
pins the SDK, and with it the runtime and the analyzer set every lane runs on
provisions every input the thorough lanes consume: the app, the HAR, the NR Editor snapshot, the browsers, the JDK
maps -p:TestProfile to a profile, and sets the build every test project inherits
the test projects themselves: runner packages, entry point, what is compiled in
the runner's parallelism and ordering, which reorders the warm chains the UI lanes exercise
the profiles the thorough lanes select their tests with
the CI definition: an edit can drop, narrow or mis-wire a lane that only the thorough jobs exercise
the composite setup action every building job runs: an edit can drop a cache, a JDK or a provisioned input that only a thorough lane consumes
the executed-at-least-one-test guard every CI test step runs through
decides whether the thorough and live lanes run at all
decides whether a skipped lane is acceptable
this list, and the jobs it names
